---
title: "Comparing the Final Armed Conflict Datasets"
format: html
---

## Purpose

This report compares `final_data.csv` with `final_data_copilot.csv`. It checks
their country-year coverage, structure, variables, and values shared between
the two datasets.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(knitr)

key <- c("iso", "year")
final_data <- read_csv("../data/processed/final_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
final_data_copilot <- read_csv(
  "../data/processed/final_data_copilot.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

original_keys <- final_data |> distinct(across(all_of(key)))
copilot_keys <- final_data_copilot |> distinct(across(all_of(key)))
common_keys <- inner_join(original_keys, copilot_keys, by = key)
```

## Dataset structure

```{r}
structure_summary <- tibble(
  dataset = c("final_data", "final_data_copilot"),
  rows = c(nrow(final_data), nrow(final_data_copilot)),
  columns = c(ncol(final_data), ncol(final_data_copilot)),
  unique_country_years = c(nrow(original_keys), nrow(copilot_keys)),
  duplicate_rows = c(
    nrow(final_data) - nrow(original_keys),
    nrow(final_data_copilot) - nrow(copilot_keys)
  )
)

kable(structure_summary, caption = "Structure of the two final datasets")
```

`final_data` has `r format(nrow(final_data), big.mark = ",")` rows but only
`r format(nrow(original_keys), big.mark = ",")` unique country-years. Thus,
it contains `r format(nrow(final_data) - nrow(original_keys), big.mark = ",")`
rows beyond one row per country-year. `final_data_copilot` has one row for each
of its `r format(nrow(copilot_keys), big.mark = ",")` country-years.

```{r}
original_multiplicity <- final_data |>
  count(across(all_of(key)), name = "rows_per_country_year")

duplicate_summary <- original_multiplicity |>
  summarise(
    country_years_with_duplicates = sum(rows_per_country_year > 1),
    maximum_rows_for_one_country_year = max(rows_per_country_year)
  )

kable(duplicate_summary, caption = "Duplicate country-years in final_data")
```

## Country-year coverage

```{r}
coverage_summary <- tibble(
  coverage = c("In both datasets", "Only in final_data", "Only in final_data_copilot"),
  country_years = c(
    nrow(common_keys),
    nrow(anti_join(original_keys, copilot_keys, by = key)),
    nrow(anti_join(copilot_keys, original_keys, by = key))
  )
)

kable(coverage_summary, caption = "Comparison of country-year coverage")

copilot_only <- anti_join(copilot_keys, original_keys, by = key)
kable(
  copilot_only |> count(year, name = "country_years") |> arrange(year),
  caption = "Years represented only in final_data_copilot"
)
```

Every country-year in `final_data` is also in `final_data_copilot`.
The copilot dataset retains an additional
`r nrow(anti_join(copilot_keys, original_keys, by = key))` country-years.

## Variables

```{r}
variable_summary <- tibble(
  category = c("Shared variables", "Only in final_data", "Only in final_data_copilot"),
  variables = c(
    paste(intersect(names(final_data), names(final_data_copilot)), collapse = ", "),
    paste(setdiff(names(final_data), names(final_data_copilot)), collapse = ", "),
    paste(setdiff(names(final_data_copilot), names(final_data)), collapse = ", ")
  )
)

kable(variable_summary, caption = "Variables available in each dataset")
```

The main substantive difference is the conflict measure. `final_data_copilot`
contains the binary `armed_conflict` indicator. `final_data` instead contains
`conflict_id` and `best`, which retain event-level conflict information and are
associated with its repeated country-years.

## Shared values

```{r}
shared_non_key <- setdiff(intersect(names(final_data), names(final_data_copilot)), key)

original_profile <- final_data |>
  semi_join(common_keys, by = key) |>
  group_by(across(all_of(key))) |>
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(shared_non_key),
      list(n_values = ~ n_distinct(.x, na.rm = FALSE), value = ~ first(.x)),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

value_comparison <- lapply(shared_non_key, function(variable) {
  compared <- original_profile |>
    select(
      all_of(key),
      n_values = all_of(paste0(variable, "_n_values")),
      original_value = all_of(paste0(variable, "_value"))
    ) |>
    inner_join(
      final_data_copilot |> select(all_of(key), copilot_value = all_of(variable)),
      by = key
    )

  tibble(
    variable,
    country_years_with_multiple_original_values = sum(compared$n_values > 1),
    mismatches_when_original_value_is_unique = sum(
      compared$n_values == 1 &
        !(is.na(compared$original_value) & is.na(compared$copilot_value)) &
        (is.na(compared$original_value) |
          is.na(compared$copilot_value) |
          compared$original_value != compared$copilot_value)
    )
  )
}) |> bind_rows()

kable(value_comparison, caption = "Shared-variable comparison across common country-years")
```

The mortality and covariate values match whenever `final_data` supplies one
value for a country-year. Earthquake and drought can have multiple values in
`final_data` for the same country-year; `final_data_copilot` instead stores one
indicator for each disaster type.

## Conclusion

`final_data_copilot` is the appropriate dataset for a country-year analysis.
It has a unique `iso`--`year` key, includes `armed_conflict`, and covers more
country-years. `final_data` should not be used interchangeably because repeated
event and disaster records inflate its row count.
